qt: to the Commission Elena Nevado del Campo (PPE) Subject:

The European Public Prosecutor’s Office has reported that it has opened a second investigation into possible fraud involving European funds earmarked for the upgrading of the Madrid-Seville high-speed railway line, where the tragic accident occurred last week in Urda with a total of 69 fatalities. The call for tenders 3.20/20810.0063 launched by ADIF for the replacement of the LZB system with the ERTMS system on the Madrid–Seville line, makes reference to the possible use of ERDF funds from the 2014–2020 Multi-regional Programme for Spain (POPE) and NextGenerationEU funds. In the Spanish Recovery, Transformation and Resilience Plan (RRP), objectives 85 and 88 include projects aimed at installing new signalling and traffic control systems (ERTMS). Given that the fact that ERTMS was not operational on the Madrid–Seville line contributed to the accident, and bearing in mind that Spain has received both ERDF funding under the 2014–2020 POPE programme and the fourth instalment of the PRTR: 1.
Can the Commission confirm whether ERDF or NextGenerationEU funds have been used to install the ERTMS system on the Madrid-Seville line?
What measures does the Commission intend to take if it is confirmed that the projects financed have not in fact been implemented?
